comment: The guidance states it serves low-, middle- and high-income settings, but the diagnosis is drawn almost entirely from LMIC experience: 'high-income' appears twice in the whole document and no high-income federated system is analysed. High-income readers will not find their problem described and may conclude the guidance is not addressed to them.

public.text: The guidance states it serves low-, middle- and high-income settings, but the diagnosis is drawn almost entirely from LMIC experience: 'high-income' appears twice in the whole document and no high-income federated system is analysed. High-income readers will not find their problem described and may conclude the guidance is not addressed to them.
public.suggestedRevision: Distinguish two fragmentation mechanisms. Programme-vertical fragmentation is the pattern the draft describes. Organisation- and market-driven fragmentation is the high-income pattern: thousands of autonomous providers, entrenched vendors, a dominant financier, several statutory regimes. The Netherlands is a clear case of the second, with high digital maturity, twenty years of standardisation and persistent discontinuity of information between providers. State that the remedies differ: the first needs shared components, the second needs an ordering framework over components that largely already exist.
